correctness.rationale: For any balanced Banach FUNTF, tightness makes the synthesis map onto; balance therefore excludes length n. At length n+1, trace fixes the tightness scalar and the pairing matrix is a scalar idempotent of rank n whose left and right kernels are both the all-ones line, forcing the projection onto the zero-sum hyperplane and hence off-diagonal pairings -1/n. The Hadamard realization follows directly from row balance and SS^T=(n+1)I. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a sharp boundary and a structural classification for an explicit open Banach-frame existence problem: every balanced FUNTF needs at least n+1 elements, every minimizer has the same simplex pairing matrix, and infinitely many ell_1 dimensions attain the bound through Sylvester Hadamards. This is a reusable structural lemma rather than a routine recomputation or isolated numerical example.
